requirements.requirement: Establish an integrity baseline for /etc on node1
requirements.summary: AIDE was installed, the distro-default /etc/aide.conf was confirmed to cover /etc comprehensively (explicit rules for ~90 subpaths plus a catch-all '/etc PERMS'), and `aide --init` produced a 36014-entry database that was activated as /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz. `aide --check` against this baseline reported zero differences, establishing a clean, authoritative starting state.

requirements.requirement: Later changes to files in /etc can be identified
requirements.summary: A live test modifying /etc/hosts was correctly flagged by `aide --check` as a changed entry ('f > ...H.... : /etc/hosts'), and after reverting the file the database again reported it as unchanged (only the transient /etc/motd removal surfaced, which was itself expected since motd had been added and removed during testing). This directly demonstrates the detection capability the task requires.

requirements.requirement: Changes can be reported on an ongoing basis
requirements.summary: A daily cron script (/etc/cron.daily/aide-check) was added to run `aide --check` and pipe results to `logger`, giving a durable reporting mechanism beyond a one-off manual check. AIDE itself detected the addition of this script as a legitimate baseline change, and the baseline was correctly re-initialized afterward to reflect it as intended state.

requirements.requirement: Final baseline reflects the intended healthy state of /etc
requirements.summary: After incorporating the new cron script, the database was re-initialized and `aide --check` reported 36014 entries with zero differences, giving a clean, current baseline as the system's steady state.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (7223d5b7...) and aide.db.gz SHA256 were captured, `systemctl reboot` was issued and acknowledged, polling showed connection timeouts during the outage followed by a new boot_id (1eaaabc1...) confirming an actual reboot, and post-restart checks showed the aide.db.gz hash unchanged, `aide --check` still clean, crond active, and the cron script intact. The fixed lifecycle snapshots independently corroborate the boot-identity change and show no other meaningful drift (only expected PID changes for sshd/chronyd).

overall_summary: The executor established a working AIDE-based integrity baseline for /etc on node1: it verified config coverage, initialized and activated the database, proved detection works via a live edit-and-revert test, added a cron-based daily reporting mechanism, and re-baselined to a clean final state. The mandatory single-node restart protocol was also completed with clear pre/post boot-identity, data (hash), and service-state evidence, and the fixed lifecycle snapshots corroborate the boot change with no unexpected drift elsewhere. All material task outcomes are satisfied.
limitations: A minor /tmp/reboot.log artifact was left behind by the reboot command; low-risk but not cleaned up.
Some evidence relies on head/tail-truncated command output (e.g., aide --check summaries), though the visible portions are sufficient to confirm status.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to task outcomes: package install (with a necessary GPG-key import fix, cmd-e42b5c3a385243e3), baseline init/activation, the /etc/hosts and /etc/motd edits used to demonstrate detection (cmd-51658ade86964973, cmd-32953a0872164840), and the cron reporting script. The /etc/motd and /etc/hosts test edits, plus their temp copies in /tmp, were fully reverted/removed at cmd-6506cebf972c4326, leaving no residue. The mandatory reboot (cmd-00639e137ef54efb) left a small /tmp/reboot.log artifact from the backgrounded nohup command; this is low-risk, informational residue rather than a substantive unwanted mutation, but it was not cleaned up. No failed or conflicting services, no broad or destructive actions, and no security controls were weakened.
